priorities.title: Grow Omnichannel Retail Across Asia Pacific
priorities.desc: Chanel is expanding its presence in Asia Pacific by linking physical boutiques with digital touchpoints. Teams need to share client data, campaign assets, and sales insights quickly across time zones. Faster collaboration tools are key to keeping the client experience consistent across every channel.
priorities.roles: Retail Operations, Sales & Client Service, Digital Marketing
priorities.pains: Slow asset sharing between HQ and boutiques; manual reporting slows decision-making; inconsistent client experience across channels

priorities.title: Deliver a Consistent Global Brand Experience
priorities.desc: Chanel must ensure that every boutique — from Paris to Singapore — reflects the same brand standards. Marketing teams produce guidelines, training materials, and campaign content that must reach thousands of staff worldwide. Misalignment leads to costly rework and brand inconsistency.
priorities.pains: Brand assets are hard to find; outdated files circulate via email; no single source of truth for brand guidelines

priorities.title: Speed Up New Product Launch Workflows
priorities.desc: Bringing a new collection or product to market involves many teams — design, legal, marketing, and operations. Approval chains are long and mostly run through email. Copilot can help compress timelines by summarising feedback, drafting content, and flagging blockers early.
priorities.pains: Long email approval chains; duplicated work across departments; late stakeholder feedback delays launch timelines

priorities.title: Develop Talent and Build AI Skills Globally
priorities.desc: Chanel is investing in its people to stay competitive in a fast-changing retail environment. HR and L&D teams are running programmes that include digital skills and AI tools. Copilot helps HR create and deliver learning content at scale across boutiques and offices.
priorities.pains: Training materials are slow to create; global scheduling across time zones is difficult; tracking completion lacks a central system

priorities.title: Advance Sustainability Reporting and Accountability
priorities.desc: Chanel has made public commitments on climate, sourcing, and supply chain transparency. Teams across operations, finance, and communications must collect data, prepare reports, and respond to stakeholder questions. Copilot can help gather and summarise sustainability data much faster.
priorities.pains: Data is scattered across teams; sustainability reports take weeks to compile; version control on shared documents is unreliable

capabilities.objectives: This group covers HQ and regional office staff who produce content, manage communications, and support day-to-day operations. They handle internal documents, coordinate across departments, and keep information flowing between teams. Their work directly supports brand quality and operational speed. They rely on Microsoft 365 for nearly every task they do.
capabilities.painPoints: Finding the right version of a document across shared drives is slow and frustrating. Email inboxes are cluttered, making it hard to track action items. Creating reports and presentations from scratch takes up significant time. Switching between Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint interrupts focus throughout the working day.
capabilities.keyActivities: drafting brand communications, preparing seasonal lookbooks, managing editorial calendars, coordinating cross-regional campaigns, reviewing and updating brand guidelines, preparing internal briefing documents

capabilities.objectives: Managers oversee teams in boutiques, regional offices, and HQ departments. They set priorities, review performance, and make decisions that affect day-to-day operations. Keeping teams aligned — especially across time zones — is a core part of their role. They also act as the link between frontline staff and senior leadership.
capabilities.painPoints: Preparing weekly status reports takes time that could be spent coaching teams. Meetings pile up without clear agendas or follow-up notes. It is hard to get a quick summary of what has happened across the team during a busy week. Approvals for campaigns, content, or spending often sit in email too long.
capabilities.keyActivities: reviewing boutique performance dashboards, preparing weekly sales reports, managing team schedules, running staff performance reviews, coordinating with regional HQ on campaign rollouts, planning seasonal stock replenishment

capabilities.objectives: Finance and operations teams manage budgets, vendor payments, inventory, and supply chain logistics. They make sure the business runs efficiently and that financial data is accurate and on time. For a company of Chanel's scale, this means handling large volumes of data across multiple regions and currencies. Both accuracy and speed matter.
capabilities.painPoints: Pulling together monthly financial reports from multiple regional inputs is time-consuming. Excel files are passed around by email, leading to version mix-ups. Tracking open purchase orders and invoice approvals requires checking multiple systems. Preparing seasonal budget forecasts involves significant manual data entry each quarter.
capabilities.keyActivities: processing and tracking purchase orders, reconciling monthly accounts across regions, preparing quarterly financial reports, monitoring inventory levels by boutique, managing vendor invoices and payment approvals, forecasting seasonal collection budgets

capabilities.objectives: HR teams manage the full employee lifecycle — from hiring and onboarding to training and performance reviews. At Chanel, they also support a strong culture of craftsmanship and brand values across a global workforce. L&D teams create programmes that help boutique staff deliver exceptional client experiences. Their work has a direct impact on client satisfaction and staff retention.
capabilities.painPoints: Creating and updating training materials is slow when done manually. Scheduling training across time zones and boutique rosters is complex and error-prone. Tracking which staff have completed required compliance training requires checking multiple lists. Writing job descriptions, onboarding packs, and HR communications from scratch takes too long.
capabilities.keyActivities: onboarding new boutique and office staff, scheduling and running training sessions, managing employee records and compliance tracking, preparing HR reports and workforce dashboards, coordinating leadership development programmes, writing job descriptions and offer letters

capabilities.objectives: Client advisors and sales staff are the face of Chanel in boutiques. They build lasting relationships with clients, handle purchases, and deliver a premium experience at every visit. In Singapore and across Asia Pacific, managing VIC relationships is especially important. Their product knowledge and client history directly drive revenue.
capabilities.painPoints: Logging client notes after a consultation is time-consuming when done manually between appointments. Finding previous client purchase history across systems slows down personalised service. Preparing for VIC appointments requires pulling information from multiple sources. Keeping up with new product knowledge across a wide range takes consistent reading time.
capabilities.keyActivities: logging client consultations and preferences in the CRM, preparing personalised client wish lists, following up on special orders and delivery status, managing VIC appointment schedules, processing in-boutique transactions, sending personalised thank-you or follow-up notes to clients

capabilities.objectives: IT teams keep Chanel's digital infrastructure running across boutiques, offices, and remote workers. They manage Microsoft 365 licences, security policies, and internal systems globally. As Chanel rolls out Copilot, IT plays a key role in deployment, access control, and staff support. Their work enables every other team to operate without disruption.
capabilities.painPoints: Supporting Microsoft 365 issues across multiple boutiques and time zones stretches the team thin. Managing user access and permissions in SharePoint is manual and prone to errors. Onboarding new devices for boutique staff takes time when done without automation. Writing clear documentation for non-technical users is time-consuming but often deprioritised.
capabilities.keyActivities: managing and assigning Microsoft 365 licences, maintaining and troubleshooting boutique POS systems, configuring security and access policies in Microsoft Entra, onboarding new devices for boutique and office staff, managing SharePoint site permissions, supporting staff with Copilot adoption queries

workflows.name: New Collection Campaign Launch

steps.d: Marketing team writes the campaign brief and shares it with all stakeholders.
Creative teams produce images, copy, and video for boutique and digital use.
Legal and brand teams review assets and send feedback via email.
Regional teams adapt content for local markets including Singapore.
Retail ops distribute final assets and briefing notes to boutique teams.

workflows.friction: Approval rounds over email are slow and hard to track. Asset versions get confused when multiple teams make edits at the same time.

workflows.name: Weekly Boutique Performance Review

steps.d: Boutique managers pull sales data from POS and CRM systems.
Managers manually compile figures into Excel or PowerPoint slides.
Regional directors review submitted reports and flag issues or trends.
Teams agree on priorities for the following week in a group meeting.

workflows.friction: Building reports manually from multiple data sources takes hours each week. Inconsistent formats across boutiques make it hard to compare results at a regional level.

workflows.name: VIC Client Consultation and Follow-up

steps.d: Client advisor reviews client history and prepares tailored product recommendations.
Advisor presents products and takes notes on client preferences during the visit.
Advisor logs visit details and follow-up items into the CRM system.
Advisor sends a personalised message or exclusive invitation to the client.

workflows.friction: Logging detailed notes after each visit is time-consuming and often done at the end of the day. Key details get missed or forgotten before they are recorded.

workflows.name: Cross-team Meeting and Decision Log

steps.d: Organiser schedules a Teams call and shares the agenda in advance.
Participants from different teams and regions join to discuss agenda topics.
One person manually takes notes while the meeting is in progress.
Organiser sends a summary email with agreed actions and owners after the meeting.

workflows.friction: Meeting notes are often incomplete and shared late. Action items get buried in email threads and are rarely tracked through to completion.

Seasonal clothing collections produced in standard sizes and sold in boutiques worldwide. RTW makes Chanel's fashion accessible to a broader luxury customer base.
An annual Chanel collection that celebrates specialist artisan workshops and their handcraft techniques. It highlights skills such as embroidery, featherwork, and jewellery-making.
A Chanel workshop in France where skilled artisans craft garments and accessories by hand. Each atelier specialises in a specific technique such as leatherwork or pleating.
The French word for 'house', used to refer to Chanel as a brand and its heritage. It signals the company's identity as a historic luxury fashion house.
A boutique sales professional who builds personal relationships with clients and guides purchases. Client Advisors are responsible for the in-store experience and repeat business.
A top-tier client who receives personalised attention, early product access, and exclusive invitations. VIC management is a key driver of revenue in luxury retail.
A set of fashion and accessories released each spring/summer or autumn/winter season. Each collection follows a creative theme set by the artistic director.
A visual catalogue of a collection's key pieces, styled and photographed for boutique and marketing use. Lookbooks guide how staff present products to clients.
The French term for craft expertise and know-how, central to Chanel's brand identity. It refers to specialist skills passed down through the ateliers over generations.
Documents that define how Chanel's logo, colours, tone, and imagery must be used. All teams must follow these to ensure a consistent brand experience globally.
The practice of arranging products and displays in boutiques to guide the client experience. Chanel HQ sets standards that boutiques worldwide must follow.
A system used to record and track client interactions, preferences, and purchase history. At Chanel, Salesforce CRM supports client advisor relationships and VIC management.
The system used in boutiques to process sales transactions and update inventory. Chanel uses Cegid Retail as its POS platform across boutiques.
An AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps that helps users draft content, summarise meetings, and find information faster. Chanel is rolling it out to improve team productivity.
Microsoft's intranet and document management platform used by Chanel for storing and sharing files. Teams use it as a central hub for policies, guidelines, and campaign assets.
Chanel's primary tool for internal messaging, video calls, and file sharing across offices and boutiques. It is the main hub for cross-regional communication.
Microsoft's cloud storage used by Chanel staff to store and share work files. It links with Teams and SharePoint for easy access from any device.
Chanel's enterprise resource planning system that manages finance, inventory, and procurement. It is the backbone of operational and financial reporting across regions.
A system that tracks a product from design through to production and retail. Fashion brands like Chanel use PLM to coordinate design, manufacturing, and commercial teams.
A retail approach that connects physical boutique and digital experiences into a seamless client journey. Chanel is expanding its omnichannel capabilities across Asia Pacific.
A framework for reporting on a company's sustainability and ethical practices. Chanel publishes ESG reports covering climate commitments, supply chain, and community impact.
The HR function responsible for training and upskilling employees across the business. At Chanel, L&D covers product knowledge, client service skills, and digital tools training.
The process of introducing and preparing new employees to work at Chanel. It covers brand values, systems training, and boutique procedures.
A regular assessment of an employee's work against agreed goals. At Chanel, these reviews support career development and inform bonus decisions.
The HR and workforce management platform used for employee records, payroll, and learning. HR teams use it to manage hiring, onboarding, and performance across regions.
Chanel's official website and e-commerce channels that represent the brand online. In Singapore, this includes the chanel.com/sg site and related digital assets.
Biannual events in Paris where Chanel presents its new seasonal collections to press and buyers. They are the most important moments in Chanel's marketing calendar.
The network of suppliers, manufacturers, and logistics partners that deliver materials and finished goods. Chanel's supply chain spans European ateliers and global distribution hubs.
The process of restocking boutique shelves when product levels fall below target. Operations teams manage this using POS data and seasonal sales forecasts.
Microsoft's identity and access management platform used by IT to control who accesses Chanel systems. It manages logins, device access, and security policies.
The process of getting staff to actively use Microsoft Copilot in their daily work. Successful adoption needs training, clear use cases, and ongoing change management support.
An employee whose main output is information — such as documents, analysis, or communications. At Chanel, this includes marketing, finance, HR, and corporate office staff.
A Microsoft 365 task management tool used by teams to track projects and actions. Chanel teams use it to manage campaign milestones and training checklists.
A document that outlines the goals, audience, and creative direction for a marketing campaign. At Chanel, briefs are created by marketing and shared with creative and regional teams.
